catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class binds the camera trigger mode and edge pair; the upstream set_trigger(mode, edge) takes both values at once, and cap.device.configure.v1 can only write named state fields.
cap.sensing.image.v1 requires an image_ref artifact, and this driver does not create one; the standard has no pixel-array carrier, so the action reports the frame width, height and count only.
No catalogue class starts continuous camera acquisition and reports the resulting trigger mode.
No catalogue class stops continuous camera acquisition and reports the resulting trigger mode.
No catalogue class closes a camera and releases its image memory as a safe-state action; cap.device.configure.v1 writes named state but does not close a device.

notes:
DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card's helper is PythonObjectDriver (python-object family); this package is a direct Driver, following the card's direct-driver decision, because decorated methods express the scalar state fields, the two-input trigger action, the capture action and the safe-state close directly. No native method or interface shape changed. The card lists five entry symbols for this multi-driver repository (UC480_Camera, PCO_Camera, LinearStage, Goniometer, TSI_Camera); this package binds the first, instrumental.drivers.cameras.uc480:UC480_Camera. NOT COVERED: the image array itself. The capture action calls grab_image and reports width, height and frame count; cap.sensing.image.v1 is not bound because returning an image_ref would need an image artifact path the driver does not create. The fake returns a 3 x 2 placeholder frame, while the real frame size follows the configured AOI (src/instrumental/drivers/cameras/uc480.py:921-923); the fake numbers are test data, not facts. trigger_delay and exposure_time are Limit.operator_required because the clone states only microsecond resolution for the trigger delay and queries the exposure range from the camera at run time (src/instrumental/drivers/cameras/uc480.py:943-946); site-limits.example.json is an example overlay, not a statement about any unit. The e-stop and the safe-state action x-cap.mabuchilab.close_camera.v1 both call the native close() (src/instrumental/drivers/cameras/uc480.py:732-752), and @reset reopens with open(). No independent hardware e-stop is cited in the clone; this is an R1 camera, so estop_physical_ref is not claimed and the loader's R2/R3 refusal of an unreviewed model-written hardware backend does not apply. The card's mock hints (remote.py:34 FakeLock, daq/ni.py:1363 VirtualDigitalChannel) are stand-ins for other driver modules, not a UC480 camera simulator; the package fake is an in-memory scalar stand-in and never loads the uc480 DLL. The package is model-authored and unreviewed, and nothing ran on hardware: the upstream module is Windows-only and needs the Thorlabs uc480 API DLL on PATH, pywin32 and nicelib (docs/uc480-cameras.rst:14-27). The final gate run had no warnings.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-10-30; reviewed_by stays null): accepted; the reviewer changed no file of the package. After the registry rebuild refreshed task.json, the reviewer re-ran the gate and wrote its digest above.
